government.note: Hereditary principality under the 1962 Constitution, described as a semi-constitutional monarchy: the Sovereign Prince holds substantial power, shares veto power with the National Council and appoints the judiciary. The Prince appoints the Minister of State, who heads the Council of Government; until a 2002 constitutional amendment the Minister had to be a French citizen proposed by France, and the Prince still consults the French Government. All legislation requires the approval of the unicameral National Council, which cannot dismiss the government.

holders.note: Regent from 31 March 2005, when the Prince's Palace announced he would take over his father's duties.
Succeeded on his father's death; investiture on 12 July 2005 and enthronement on 19 November 2005.

system.note: In 1998 the 18 seats were elected by a two-round majority system with panachage in a single national constituency (a majority of valid votes needed in the first round). From the 2003 election the Council has 24 seats: 16 by plurality block voting and 8 by list proportional representation among lists above 5%. seats_2000 is the February 1998 result.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Derived from the February 1998 National Council first-round vote shares (candidate votes under panachage): National and Democratic Union 67.40% (conservative, monarchist; traditional conservative), National Union for the Future of Monaco 23.38% (centrist, monarchist) and Rally for the Monegasque Family 9.21% (both mapped to constitutional monarchist). All Monegasque parties support the monarchy.
